- ok put these instructions at the end of log.md

### Changes
- Appended deployment checklist for VM/nginx relay config.

### Deployment Checklist (VM)
1) Pull latest repo changes on the VM.
2) Generate the relay config file from the repo root:
```
bash scripts/start-relay-prod.sh
```
3) Ensure nginx can read the config file (keep identity key private):
```
chmod 755 /home/cos /home/cos/projects /home/cos/projects/peercompute /home/cos/projects/peercompute/config
chmod 644 /home/cos/projects/peercompute/config/relay-config.json
chmod 600 /home/cos/projects/peercompute/config/relay-peer-id.json
```
4) Update the nginx alias to the repo path:
```
location = /peercompute/config/relay-config.json {
    alias /home/cos/projects/peercompute/config/relay-config.json;
    default_type application/json;
    add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin *;
    add_header Cache-Control "no-store";
}
```
5) Reload nginx:
```
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```
6) Verify the config URL loads:
- `https://secretworkshop.net/peercompute/config/relay-config.json`

## Date: 2025-01-01

### Prompt
- ok you made some progress but we're back to getting the streamstateerror. and nodes spawn on top of eachother.

### Changes
- Added metricInitialized tracking to presence + telemetry payloads so NetViz can treat zero metrics as uninitialized and fall back to spiral placement.

## Date: 2026-01-01

### Prompt (original scope)
> "hey Codex. please review all plan/log files. especially the current-branch.md we're working on moving over to gossipsub and webrtc for our network stack but we're running into some problems with topology of the network, stability of the relay server over long periods (the relay stops working after a while and nodes end up isolated though the relay log shows they are connecting), the relay is also crashing occasionally after trying to publish to a closed stream. I think too many messages in general are being sent on the p2p network in the netviz. I believe this is because the global state for every single node is being broadcast for the entire network. to solve this I think we need to move to a sharded global state model where each node only needs to know the state of peers in its vicinity.
>
> I think it's time to move to the explicit topologies identified in the topologies image to help with heirarchical organization and fix these bugs in an organized way.
>
> come up with a detailed plan that includes a node resident algorithm for determining which peers it needs to dial and connect to depending on the topology.
>
> for the fully distributed topology, each game or workload is expected to provide a metic which can be used to determine where that node is placed in the topology. for a game in an expansive 3d world this could be based on player location and the player would connect only to the n nodes that are physically closest to it in the virtual world. for a fully distributed computational workload this metric could be based on the actual problem space the node is assigned, and they would connect to the n nodes that are nearest them in the problem space.
>
> in any fully distributed topology nodes must have target connection count (which it will try to settle at) and a maximum connection count. New nodes should be placed near the edge of the network and prefer connecting to nodes that are below their target connection limit. Come up with or find a robust provably bug free algorithm to facilitate this.
>
> We need to be able to select a topology in the netviz app. this must be a separate abstraction above "room" because a single topology (like the heirarchical model) may have multiple rooms within it that will need to be visualized globally in the netviz.
>
> in the netviz for the fully distributed topology let the user move their cube around the grid which should trigger connections to other nodes. by default the cubes should be arranged in a square pattern with new nodes being placed around the edge in a spiral pattern.
>
> come up with runtime and unit tests you can use to validate the functionality and check for errors and fix them without requiring me to tell you.
>
> for the heirarchical topology the room hosts will be selected by compute power and bandwidth. a node can choose to join a room that is not full, or start a new room. when a host node disconnects, the nodes need to come up with an algorithm for choosing and promoting a new host themselves. look for existing provably safe and reliable algorithms for achieving this. perhapps by having a warmed up "backup host" node ready to take over should the primary host disconnect.
>
> the netviz implementation of this should look something like the heirarchical network in the topology diagram. after opening the netviz page and selecting the heirarchical topology they should be presented with an overview of the entire network showing all hosts and how many client nodes are connected to each host (but without the live data from each room) if a room is not fully a user should be able to click on a host node to join their node to that host.
>
> For the ad hoc or emergent network topology I'd like you to come up with a strategy and stub it out. I suspect we won't know how to approach that until we have completed the other two topologies.
>
> add all of this to the branch plan and lets dig in!"

### Changes
- Added gossipsub outbound stream patching in NetworkManager to catch async send failures from YamuxStream, drop the offending pubsub peer, and hang up the connection to avoid repeated StreamStateError spam.
- Added pubsub stream error throttling to reduce log spam while still surfacing failures.
- Added joinedAt to telemetry snapshots so NetViz can determine which peer connected last.
- NetViz now resolves metric collisions by relocating the most recently joined peer to the next available spiral coordinate and logs the move.
- Updated plan/branch/topologies.md to reflect the new gossipsub stream patch and progress update.
- Rebuilt NetViz docs assets after the NetViz changes.

run_case() {
  local label="$1"
  shift

  local relay_log="/tmp/pc-relay-${label}.log"
  local static_log="/tmp/p2p-static-${label}.log"
  local test_log="/tmp/p2p-relay-scale-${label}.log"
  local relay_pid=""
  local static_pid=""
  cleanup() {
    if [ -n "${static_pid}" ]; then kill "${static_pid}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
    if [ -n "${relay_pid}" ]; then kill "${relay_pid}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
    wait >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  }
  trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

  RELAY_CONFIG_DIRS=dist RELAY_LISTEN_HOST=127.0.0.1 RELAY_LISTEN_PORT=0 RELAY_PUBLIC_HOST=127.0.0.1 \
    node src/relay/server.js >"${relay_log}" 2>&1 &
  relay_pid=$!

  static_pid=$!

  sleep 1

  echo "[p2p-relay-scale] run ${label}"
  set +e
  eval "USE_EXISTING_SERVER=1 P2P_SCALE_NODE_COUNT=15 P2P_SCALE_START_DELAY_MS=3000 P2P_SCALE_SETTLE_MS=20000 P2P_SCALE_LOG_PAGES=0 P2P_SCALE_MAX_PARALLEL_DIALS=8 P2P_SCALE_MAX_DIAL_PEERS=8 ${extra_env} npx playwright test tests/p2p-relay-scale.spec.js --reporter=line | tee '${test_log}'"
  local status=$?
  set -e

  cleanup
  trap - EXIT INT TERM
  echo "[p2p-relay-scale] ${label} exit ${status}"
  return ${status}
}

set -e
run_case "01-baseline" ""
BASELINE_STATUS=$?
run_case "02-no-state" "P2P_SCALE_DISABLE_PERSISTENCE=1 P2P_SCALE_DISABLE_STATE_SYNC=1"

printf "\\n[p2p-relay-scale] summary baseline=%s no_state=%s conn_caps=%s\\n" "${BASELINE_STATUS}" "${NO_STATE_STATUS}" "${CONN_STATUS}"'

## Date: 2026-01-02

### Prompt
> can you search the web to see if you can find anything?  maybe the relay server is blocking our connections so a single IP can't flood the network

### Changes
- Web research: circuit-relay v2 relies on reservations; relays can reject reservations when resources are exhausted (RESERVATION_REFUSED) or when ACL filters apply.
- go-libp2p relay resources include per-IP/per-ASN reservation caps (MaxReservationsPerIP/MaxReservationsPerASN), so IP-based throttling is possible in go relays.
- js-libp2p circuit-relay-v2 server defaults to maxReservations=15 with data/time limits, so a ~10-15 node cap matches the default js relay behavior rather than explicit IP blocking.

- plan/log.md

- Reviewed local js-libp2p circuit-relay-v2 defaults: maxReservations=15, reservationClearInterval=300000ms, reservationTtl=7200000ms (2h).

### Implementation Details
Phase 1 adds relay as gossipsub directPeer:
- DirectPeers are permanently maintained in gossipsub mesh by libp2p
- Relay receives all pubsub messages even from peers who dropped relay connection
- Relay can forward messages between NAT-restricted peers and direct-connected peers
- New peers joining via relay can discover all existing peers
- Prevents "one-way door" problem where new peers couldn't find peers who left relay

Config option:
```javascript
{
  enableRelayDirectPeers: true,  // default, set false to disable
  gossipsub: {
    directPeers: [/* auto-populated from bootstrapPeers */]
  }
}
```

- Ran headless NetViz scale tests at 10, 20, and 30 peers to validate Phase 1 relay scaling.

### Commands
- node /home/cos/projects/peercompute/peercompute/tests/runtime/netviz-scale.mjs --peers 10 --settle 20000

### Tests
- All scale tests passed (harness completed without error).

### Results

| Peers | Min Visible | Avg Visible | Max Visible | Avg Connections | Relay Connected |
|-------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| 10    | 3           | 3.70        | 5           | 4.70            | 10              |
| 20    | 1           | 1.10        | 2           | 1.10            | 20              |
| 30    | 1           | 1.07        | 2           | 1.07            | 30              |

### Analysis

**Phase 1 (Gossipsub directPeers)**: ✓ WORKING
- All peers successfully connected to relay at all scales (10/10, 20/20, 30/30).
- Relay stays in gossipsub mesh via directPeers configuration.
- No mesh fragmentation observed; relay can forward messages between all peers.

**Phase 3 (Relay Retention)**: ⚠️ NOT VALIDATED
- `dropRelayBootstrapOnDirect` defaults to `false` in NetViz config.
- All peers keep their relay connection, so retention selection logic never triggers.
- To validate Phase 3, must enable `dropRelayBootstrapOnDirect: true` and set `relayRetention` mode.

**Peer Visibility (Distributed Topology)**:
- Low peer counts are expected behavior for distributed topology with:
  - `targetConnections: 3`, `maxConnections: 5`
  - `connectionRadius: 1.2` (metric-space neighbor selection)
- At 10 peers: avg 3.7 visible ≈ targetConnections (working as designed).
- At 20+ peers: visibility degrades to ~1 peer, indicating:
  - Spiral placement spreads peers beyond connectionRadius.
  - Not enough convergence time for topology controller to reach steady state.
  - May need to increase connectionRadius or settle time for larger scales.

### Recommendations

1. **Phase 3 Validation**: Add a separate test with `dropRelayBootstrapOnDirect: true` and `relayRetention: { mode: 'sqrt', min: 2, max: 5 }` to verify retention logic.

2. **Scale Improvements**: For 20+ peers with distributed topology:
   - Increase `connectionRadius` (e.g., 2.0-3.0) to span more of the spiral.
   - Increase settle time (60s+) for topology convergence.
   - Consider grid or random placement instead of spiral for scale tests.

3. **Topology Tuning**: Current distributed topology is designed for locality-aware connections. For global visibility tests, use `topologyType: hierarchical` or disable topology controller.

### Prompt

### Analysis
- Peer scoring is NOT the cause - gossipsub peer scoring is not configured.
- Root cause: TopologyController's `connectionRadius: 1.2` combined with spiral placement.
- Spiral placement spreads peers ~1 unit apart; 20th peer is ~4-5 units from origin.
- Peers beyond connectionRadius are filtered from connection candidates.

## Date: 2026-01-22 (Phase 2 Implementation)

### Prompt
- proceed with phase 2 (separate control/data planes)

### Changes

**Implemented relay control-only mode** (`RELAY_CONTROL_ONLY_MODE` env variable):

1. **Relay Server Changes** (peercompute/src/relay/server.js):
   - Added `relayControlOnlyMode` flag from env variable
   - Added control topics list: discovery, presence, direct
   - Added data topics list: state, state-sync
   - Added `isDataTopic()` function to detect state/shard topics
   - Modified topic subscription to skip data topics in control-only mode
   - Added logging: "Control-only mode enabled - skipping state topic subscriptions"

2. **Test Harness Updates** (peercompute/tests/runtime/netviz-scale.mjs):
   - Added `--controlOnly` flag to enable control-only mode
   - Added `RELAY_CONTROL_ONLY_MODE` to relay env when flag is set
   - Added log output for control-only mode status

### Analysis

**Rationale**: NAT-restricted peers get state through WebRTC connections facilitated by relay signaling (STUN/TURN), not through relay pubsub. The relay only needs to handle:
- Discovery (peer announcements)
- Presence (who's online)
- Direct signaling (WebRTC offer/answer/ICE)

State sync flows directly between peers over WebRTC, so relay doesn't need to subscribe to those topics.

### Validation

Ran `node netviz-scale.mjs --peers 4 --controlOnly true`:
```
[Relay] Control-only mode enabled - skipping state topic subscriptions
Relay subscribed to topics: peercompute._peer-discovery._p2p._pubsub, peercompute-presence, peercompute-direct
[Relay] Skipping data topic (control-only mode): pc.netviz-scale.scale.state
```

Results:
- ✅ Relay only subscribes to control topics
- ✅ State topics correctly skipped
- ✅ Discovery announcements flow normally
- ✅ All 4 peers discovered and connected

### Conclusion

**Phase 2**: ✅ COMPLETED
- Control/data plane separation implemented
- Relay can now run in lightweight mode handling only signaling
- Reduces relay bandwidth by not forwarding state sync traffic
- Ready for production deployment with `RELAY_CONTROL_ONLY_MODE=true`

## Date: 2026-01-22 (Phase 4 & 5 Implementation)

### Prompt
- lets do phase 4 and 5

### Changes

**Phase 4: Reconnect-on-Demand for Dialing**

1. **Config Options** (NetworkManager.js `normalizeWebRTCConfig()`):
   - `reconnectOnDialFailure` (default: true) - enable feature
   - `reconnectThrottleMs` (default: 30000) - min time between reconnects
   - `autoDropRelayAfterDialMs` (default: 60000) - auto-drop relay after dial (0 to disable)

2. **State Tracking** (NetworkManager constructor):
   ```javascript
   this.relayReconnectState = {
     lastReconnectAt: 0,
     pendingDialsNeedingRelay: new Set(),
     autoDisconnectTimer: null
   };
   ```

3. **New Methods**:
   - `_shouldReconnectRelayForDial(peerId)` - checks throttle, relay status, feature flag
   - `_reconnectRelayForDial(peerId)` - calls `_dialBootstrapPeers()`, returns success/fail
   - `_buildCircuitAddr(peerId)` - constructs `/p2p-circuit/p2p/{peerId}` multiaddr
   - `_scheduleAutoRelayDrop()` - drops relay 60s after successful dial

4. **Integration** (in `_maybeDialPeer()`):
   - After all direct addresses fail, if relay not connected
   - Call `_reconnectRelayForDial(peerId)`
   - If reconnected, dial via circuit relay
   - Schedule auto-drop timer

**Phase 5: Enhanced Peer Directory**

1. **Relay Implementation** (server.js):
   - `RELAY_ENABLE_DIRECTORY` env var (default: true)
   - `RELAY_DIRECTORY_TTL_MS` env var (default: 5 min)
   - `peerDirectory` Map stores `{ multiaddrs, lastSeen, roomId, topologyId, shardId }`
   - Populated from presence messages
   - `handleDirectoryQuery()` responds to queries
   - Handles `directory-register` for explicit registration
   - Periodic cleanup every 60s

2. **Client Implementation** (NetworkManager.js):
   - `enablePeerDirectory` config (default: true)
   - `directoryTopic` config (default: 'peercompute-directory')
   - `directoryQueryTimeoutMs` config (default: 5000)

## Date: 2026-02-10

### Prompt (2026-02-10 19:55:05 UTC)
- "ok proceed"

### Actions Taken
- Re-read planning context before changes:
  - `plan/plan.md`
  - `plan/log.md`
- Re-traced containernet topology + harness code paths and confirmed two concrete root-cause bugs for the matrix preflight failures:
  1. Host seeding ordering bug:
     - `_seed_agent_hosts()` was called before `self._agents`/`self._agent_index` were assigned in `_start_containernet()`, so no agents were iterated and no service host mappings were written to `/etc/hosts`.
  2. Interface targeting bug:
     - `_configure_agent()` and `_configure_service()` hardcoded `eth0`.
     - In containernet docker nodes, the data-plane Mininet interface is the node-attached interface (e.g., `agent-01-eth0`), not necessarily Docker bridge `eth0`.
     - This can route traffic incorrectly and cause HTTPS fallback IP probes to time out even when services are up.
- Implemented topology fixes:
  - In `_start_containernet()`, set `self._agents` and `self._agent_index` immediately after agent allocation and before host seeding.
  - Changed `_seed_agent_hosts()` to accept an explicit agent list (`agents: Iterable[AgentRecord] | None`) and called it as `_seed_agent_hosts(agents)` from startup flow.
  - Added `_node_data_interface()` helper that picks the first non-loopback interface from `node.intfNames()` with `eth0` fallback.
  - Updated `_configure_agent()` and `_configure_service()` to use `_node_data_interface(...)` instead of hardcoded `eth0`.
- Implemented harness diagnostics fix:
  - Removed `|| true` masking from:
    - hosts lookup command (`grep -F -- <host> /etc/hosts`)
    - fallback route checks (`ip route get` / `ip -6 route get`)
  - This preserves meaningful `hosts_rc` and `route_to_fallback_rc` values in preflight diagnostics.
- Updated tests:
  - Adjusted fake topology command matchers for the stricter grep command.
  - Added `test_node_data_interface_prefers_mininet_intf`.
  - Added `test_configure_agent_uses_data_interface`.
  - Added `test_seed_agent_hosts_accepts_explicit_agent_list`.
- Updated test strategy documentation in `plan/tests.md` with new containernet expectations:
  - data-plane interface selection requirement,
  - host seeding ordering requirement,
  - route diagnostic non-masking requirement.

- #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
python_bin="${PYTHON_BIN:-/home/$USER/projects/containernet/.venv/bin/python}"
matrix_config="$repo_root/net-chaos-lab/configs/matrix/direct-regression.yaml"

pick_free_port() {
  python3 - <<'PY'
import socket
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
print(s.getsockname()[1])
s.close()
PY
}

cleanup_stale_netviz_listener() {
  local port="$1"
  if ! command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return
  fi
  local removed=0
  while IFS= read -r pid; do
    [[ -z "${pid:-}" ]] && continue
    local cmdline
    cmdline="$(ps -p "$pid" -o args= 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$cmdline" == *"demos/netviz"* || "$cmdline" == *"vite"* ]]; then
      kill "$pid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      removed=$((removed + 1))
      echo "[chaos-lab] removed stale NetViz listener on :$port (pid=$pid)"
    fi
  done < <(lsof -tiTCP:"$port" -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null || true)
  if (( removed > 0 )); then
    sleep 0.4
  fi
}

wait_for_netviz_chaos_api() {
  local url="$1"
  local retries="${2:-40}"
  for _ in $(seq 1 "$retries"); do
    local code
    code="$(curl -k -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)"
    if [[ "$code" == "200" ]]; then
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 0.25
  done
  return 1
}

ensure_sudo_ready() {
  if sudo -n true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
    echo "[chaos-lab] sudo requires an interactive terminal for matrix:full." >&2
    echo "[chaos-lab] run this command directly in your shell and enter your sudo password when prompted." >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "[chaos-lab] requesting sudo for containernet matrix execution..."
  sudo -v
}

ensure_sudo_ready

dashboard_host="${CHAOS_DASHBOARD_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
if [[ -n "${CHAOS_DASHBOARD_PORT:-}" ]]; then
  dashboard_port="${CHAOS_DASHBOARD_PORT}"
else
  dashboard_port="$(pick_free_port)"
fi
netviz_host="${CHAOS_NETVIZ_HOST:-0.0.0.0}"
netviz_port="${CHAOS_NETVIZ_PORT:-5182}"

chaos_api_base="${CHAOS_NETVIZ_API_BASE:-/chaos-api}"
chaos_proxy_target="${CHAOS_NETVIZ_PROXY_TARGET:-http://${dashboard_host}:${dashboard_port}}"
chaos_api_encoded="$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(encodeURIComponent(process.argv[1] || ""))' "$chaos_api_base")"
watch_query="room=telemetry&topologyId=netviz-topology&topologyType=distributed&render=low&dropRelay=true&relayRetentionMode=sqrt&relayRetentionMin=2&autoConnect=0&chaosApi=${chaos_api_encoded}"
watch_url_override="${CHAOS_NETVIZ_WATCH_URL:-}"

netviz_log="$repo_root/net-chaos-lab/artifacts/netviz-watch.log"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$netviz_log")"
: >"$netviz_log"

cleanup_stale_netviz_listener "$netviz_port"

netviz_command="${CHAOS_NETVIZ_COMMAND:-npm --prefix \"$repo_root/demos/netviz\" run dev -- --host ${netviz_host} --port ${netviz_port} --strictPort}"

echo "[chaos-lab] launching NetViz watcher..."
echo "[chaos-lab] netviz command: $netviz_command"
echo "[chaos-lab] netviz log: $netviz_log"
echo "[chaos-lab] dashboard port: $dashboard_port"

PEERCOMPUTE_NO_OPEN=1 DEV_OPEN_OVERVIEW=0 VITE_CHAOS_API_PROXY_TARGET="$chaos_proxy_target" bash -lc "$netviz_command" >>"$netviz_log" 2>&1 &
netviz_pid=$!

cleanup() {
  if [[ -n "${netviz_pid:-}" ]] && kill -0 "$netviz_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    kill "$netviz_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    wait "$netviz_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

sleep 2
if ! kill -0 "$netviz_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[chaos-lab] failed to keep NetViz running; recent log lines:" >&2
  tail -n 40 "$netviz_log" >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi

actual_netviz_port="$netviz_port"
for _ in {1..30}; do
  local_url="$(rg -o 'https://localhost:[0-9]+' "$netviz_log" | tail -n 1 || true)"
  if [[ -n "$local_url" ]]; then
    actual_netviz_port="${local_url##*:}"
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

if [[ -n "$watch_url_override" ]]; then
  watch_url="$watch_url_override"
else
  watch_url="https://localhost:${actual_netviz_port}/?${watch_query}"
fi

if [[ "$actual_netviz_port" != "$netviz_port" ]]; then
  echo "[chaos-lab] note: requested NetViz port ${netviz_port} was busy; using ${actual_netviz_port}."
fi

echo "[chaos-lab] open NetViz watcher URL:"
echo "  $watch_url"
echo "[chaos-lab] netviz chaos proxy target: $chaos_proxy_target"

chaos_probe_url="https://localhost:${actual_netviz_port}${chaos_api_base}/api/summary"
if ! wait_for_netviz_chaos_api "$chaos_probe_url"; then
  echo "[chaos-lab] NetViz chaos-api preflight failed at $chaos_probe_url (expected HTTP 200)." >&2
  echo "[chaos-lab] recent NetViz log lines:" >&2
  tail -n 60 "$netviz_log" >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi

cmd=(

)
if [[ "$#" -gt 0 ]]; then
  cmd+=("$@")
fi

def run_single(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any], Path]:
  root = repo_root()
  run_id = str(args.run_id or '').strip() or default_run_id()
  artifacts_root = Path(args.artifacts_root).expanduser().resolve()
  run_dir = artifacts_root / run_id
  run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  topology_state_path = run_dir / 'chaos-topology.json'

  metrics = MetricsStore(artifacts_dir=run_dir, run_id=run_id)
  metrics.record(
    'run_started',
    {
      'run_id': run_id,
      'topology_config': str(args.topology),
      'scenario_config': str(args.scenario),
      'mode': args.mode,
    },
  )
  metrics.build_summary()

  try:
    topology_loaded = load_topology_config(args.topology)
    scenario_loaded = load_scenario_config(args.scenario)
  except ConfigError as exc:
    metrics.record('run_failed', {'error': f'config: {exc}'})
    summary = metrics.build_summary()
    print(f'[chaos-lab] config error: {exc}')
    print('[chaos-lab] summary:')
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(f'[chaos-lab] artifacts: {run_dir}')
    return 2, summary, run_dir

  topology_cfg = dict(topology_loaded.data)
  if args.agents:
    topology_cfg.setdefault('agents', {})
    topology_cfg['agents']['count'] = max(1, min(50, int(args.agents)))

  topology = ChaosTopology(
    config=topology_cfg,
    repo_root=root,
    artifacts_dir=run_dir,
    mode=args.mode,
    logger=print,
  )
  harness = ChaosHarness(
    repo_root=root,
    topology=topology,
    metrics=metrics,
    artifacts_dir=run_dir,
    logger=print,
  )

  latest_stage: dict[str, Any] | None = None
  dashboard_server = None
  dashboard_thread: threading.Thread | None = None
  if args.dashboard:
    try:
      dashboard_server = create_dashboard_server(
        host=args.dashboard_host,
        port=int(args.dashboard_port),
        summary_path=metrics.paths.summary_json,
        events_path=metrics.paths.events_jsonl,
        static_dir=root / 'net-chaos-lab' / 'dashboard',
        topology_path=topology_state_path,
      )
      print(f'[dashboard] listening on http://{args.dashboard_host}:{int(args.dashboard_port)}')
      dashboard_thread = threading.Thread(
        target=dashboard_server.serve_forever,
        daemon=True,
        name='chaoslab-dashboard',
      )
      dashboard_thread.start()
    except OSError as exc:
      print(f'[chaos-lab] dashboard unavailable: {exc}')
      metrics.record('dashboard_start_failed', {'error': str(exc)})

  harness_cfg = topology_cfg.get('harness', {})
  probe_url = str(args.url or harness_cfg.get('default_url') or 'https://demos.peercompute.test/netviz/')
  min_peers = int(args.min_peers or harness_cfg.get('min_expected_peers') or 2)
  wait_ms = int(args.wait_ms or harness_cfg.get('probe_duration_ms') or 30000)
  probe_agents = int(args.probe_agents or 0)
  probe_parallelism = max(1, int(args.probe_parallelism or 4))

  def run_probe_checkpoint(label: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    results = harness.run_probe_cycle(
      url=probe_url,
      min_peers=min_peers,
      wait_ms=wait_ms,
      mode=str(harness_cfg.get('default_demo') or 'netviz'),
      media=bool(args.media),
      limit_agents=probe_agents,
      parallelism=probe_parallelism,
    )
    metrics.record('probe_checkpoint', {'label': label, 'results': len(results)})
    metrics.build_summary()
    if bool(args.probe_fail_fast) and results:
      infra_failures = sum(1 for payload in results if bool(payload.get('infra_failure')))
      if infra_failures >= len(results):
        raise RuntimeError(
          f'probe fail-fast triggered at checkpoint "{label}": '
          f'{infra_failures}/{len(results)} probes reported infra_failure'
        )
    return results

  exit_code = 0
  summary: dict[str, Any] = {}
  try:
    if not args.skip_probes and str(args.mode).strip().lower() != 'dry-run':
      _ensure_netviz_docs_bundle(root, logger=print)
    topology.start()
    _write_topology_state(topology_state_path, run_id, topology, latest_stage=None)
    metrics.record(
      'topology_started',
      {
        'actual_mode': topology.actual_mode,
        'agent_count': len(topology.list_agents()),
        'service_count': len(topology.list_services()),
      },
    )

    if args.demo_command:
      demo_cwd = Path(args.demo_cwd).expanduser().resolve() if args.demo_cwd else root
      harness.start_demo(args.demo_command, cwd=demo_cwd)

    if not args.skip_probes:
      run_probe_checkpoint('initial')

    if not args.skip_scenario:
      def stage_callback(outcome: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        nonlocal latest_stage
        latest_stage = dict(outcome)
        _write_topology_state(topology_state_path, run_id, topology, latest_stage=latest_stage)
        if args.skip_probes:
          return
        if not args.probe_each_stage:
          return
        phase = str(outcome.get('phase') or 'stage')
        index = int(outcome.get('stage_index') or 0)
        run_probe_checkpoint(f'{phase}-{index}')

      runner = ScenarioRunner(
        topology=topology,
        metrics=metrics,
        logger=print,
        time_scale=float(args.time_scale),
        on_stage_result=stage_callback,
      )
      runner.run(scenario_loaded.data)

    if not args.skip_probes:
      run_probe_checkpoint('final')

  except (TopologyError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
    exit_code = 1
    metrics.record('run_failed', {'error': str(exc)})
    print(f'[chaos-lab] failure: {exc}')
  except KeyboardInterrupt:
    exit_code = 130
    metrics.record('run_interrupted', {'reason': 'keyboard-interrupt'})
    print('[chaos-lab] interrupted')
  finally:
    try:
      _write_topology_state(topology_state_path, run_id, topology, latest_stage=latest_stage)
    except Exception:
      pass
    harness.stop_demo()
    topology.stop()
    if dashboard_server is not None:
      try:
        dashboard_server.shutdown()
      except Exception:
        pass
      try:
        dashboard_server.server_close()
      except Exception:
        pass
      if dashboard_thread is not None:
        dashboard_thread.join(timeout=2.0)
    summary = metrics.build_summary()
    print('[chaos-lab] summary:')
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(f'[chaos-lab] artifacts: {run_dir}')

  return exit_code, summary, run_dir


def _matrix_value(
  run_spec: Any,
  defaults: dict[str, Any],
  key: str,
  fallback: Any,
) -> Any:
  if key in run_spec.overrides:
    return run_spec.overrides[key]
  if key in defaults:
    return defaults[key]

      + (f'\n{detail}' if detail else '')
    )
  logger('[chaos-lab] NetViz docs bundle refreshed.')


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
  root = repo_root()
  parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='PeerCompute network chaos-lab runner')

  parser.add_argument(
    '--topology',
    default=str(root / 'net-chaos-lab' / 'configs' / 'topology.default.yaml'),
    help='Path to topology yaml/json config',
  )
  parser.add_argument(
    '--scenario',
    default=str(root / 'net-chaos-lab' / 'configs' / 'scenarios' / 'default-chaos.yaml'),
    help='Path to scenario yaml/json config',
  )
  parser.add_argument('--mode', default='auto', choices=['auto', 'containernet', 'dry-run'])
  parser.add_argument('--agents', type=int, default=0, help='Override number of browser agents (1-50)')

  parser.add_argument('--run-id', default='', help='Override run id')
  parser.add_argument(
    '--artifacts-root',
    default=str(root / 'net-chaos-lab' / 'artifacts'),
    help='Root directory for artifacts/run outputs',
  )

  parser.add_argument('--demo-command', default='', help='Optional command to start a demo server')
  parser.add_argument('--demo-cwd', default='', help='Working directory for demo command')

  parser.add_argument('--url', default='', help='Probe URL override')
  parser.add_argument('--min-peers', type=int, default=0, help='Minimum peers required for probe pass')
  parser.add_argument('--wait-ms', type=int, default=0, help='Probe wait timeout override in ms')
  parser.add_argument('--probe-agents', type=int, default=0, help='How many agents to probe per cycle')
  parser.add_argument('--probe-parallelism', type=int, default=4)
  parser.add_argument('--probe-each-stage', action='store_true')
  parser.add_argument('--skip-probes', action='store_true')
  parser.add_argument('--media', action='store_true', help='Enable audio/video loopback probe')
  parser.add_argument(
    '--probe-fail-fast',
    dest='probe_fail_fast',
    action='store_true',
    default=False,
    help='Abort run when a probe checkpoint reports infra failure for all probed agents',
  )

- Searched CubeChat startup/welcome overlay handlers and found the issue in `demos/cubechat/src/main.js`:
  - mobile path only listened for `click`,
  - desktop path dismissed the overlay only after successful `pointerlockchange`,
  - direct unguarded `requestPointerLock()` / `exitPointerLock()` calls could fail on Safari/WebKit variants.
- Implemented a startup interaction hardening patch for Apple browsers:
  - added mobile/touch detection helper that treats iPadOS desktop-mode UA (`MacIntel` + touch points) as mobile-like,
  - added WebKit-safe pointer-lock helpers (`webkitRequestPointerLock`, `webkitExitPointerLock`, `webkitPointerLockElement` fallback),
  - added a shared overlay start handler with `click` + `pointerdown` + `touchend` support and duplicate-trigger guard,
  - made overlay dismissal independent from pointer-lock success so Safari/iOS users are not blocked,
  - preserved desktop pointer-lock behavior by keeping canvas click pointer-lock requests and auto-exiting only for the initial welcome/start gesture.
- Improved welcome overlay accessibility/interaction ergonomics:
  - added `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, keyboard activation (`Enter`/`Space`),
  - added CSS `touch-action: manipulation`, disabled tap highlight, and `user-select: none`.
- Updated `plan/tests.md` with a CubeChat manual regression checklist for Safari/iOS startup overlay behavior.

2. Trinary star equilateral triangle: ang = (i/3)*PI*2 with tangential velocity (-sin(ang)*v, 0, cos(ang)*v)
3. Shader `isPerspectiveMatrix` fixes: added `#include <common>` before `#include <logdepthbuf_pars_vertex>` in asteroid belt, comet particle, ring system shaders
4. BH disk logdepthbuf: full include chain in both vertex and fragment shaders; removed depthTest:false
5. Planet y-offset spawn: yOff = (rand()-0.5)*dist*0.05; asteroid y-spread 0.03->0.12
6. Kuiper belt (2000 icy particles, 3-ring indicator group), Oort cloud (1800 sphere particles, wireframe shell)
7. Asteroid belt ring indicator (LineLoop), all toggled with orbit paths checkbox
8. Comet orbitTrailLine stored in body object; passiveBodies forEach in toggle handler
9. Moon orbit trails: LineLoop circle per moon, re-centered each frame on parent planet
10. Asteroid/Kuiper selectability, raycaster threshold=10, click handler extended
11. isLandable: GAS GIANT removed; MOON/ASTEROID/KUIPER added; button text variants
12. generatePlanetSurface: isSmallBody/isMoon detection, scaled R/heightScale/gravity/colors/atmosphere
13. addQuasarJets: age-based jets+halo at young galaxy ages (ageFactor > 0.05)

- User reported runtime still has occasional isolation/collapse and supplied long logs showing:
  - bootstrap peer open/close flapping (`12D3KooWN8...`),

### Prompt Time/Date
- 2026-03-01T04:02:58Z

### Actions Attempted
- Analyzed relay control flow and identified a logic conflict between:
  - relay redial election (`_shouldElectRelayRedial`) and
  - drop policy (`dropRelayBootstrapOnDirect` + `_shouldKeepRelayBootstrapConnection`).
- Root cause:
  - elected node can redial bootstrap when disconnected,
  - then immediately drop bootstrap on the next tick because drop policy executes without honoring election keeper role,
  - producing open/close ping-pong and unstable reservation state.
- Implemented fix:
  - `_maybeUpdateBootstrapRelayConnections` now computes bootstrap state + election once per tick.
  - if elected keeper and bootstrap is absent -> redial.
  - if elected keeper and bootstrap is present -> keep it (do not drop).
  - drop-policy path now only executes when node is not elected keeper.
  - `_shouldElectRelayRedial` extended with `allowWithBootstrap` option to support keeper decision while connected.
- Added unit regression coverage:
  - `NetworkManager keeps bootstrap relay when elected keeper even with direct peers`.
- Updated test strategy checklist to include the new test.
